bullets.title: Foundations of Recovery-Oriented Mental Health Nursing
bullets.text: Mental health nursing recognises the person beyond diagnosis. Recovery does not always mean the complete absence of symptoms. It may mean living a meaningful, hopeful and self-directed life while managing ongoing challenges. Nurses support recovery by listening, respecting choice, identifying strengths and reducing…

bullets.title: Therapeutic Communication and Professional Relationships
bullets.text: The therapeutic relationship is central to mental health nursing. It is purposeful, time-limited and focused on the person's needs. Trust develops through consistency, empathy, honesty and clear boundaries.

bullets.title: Mental Health Assessment and Common Conditions
bullets.text: A mental health assessment combines the person's story, observed behaviour, mental state, physical health and current risks. The assessment should be collaborative and should not reduce the person to a checklist.

bullets.title: Crisis, Safety and Psychotropic Medication
bullets.text: Mental health crises may involve suicidal thoughts, self-harm, aggression, severe withdrawal, panic, mania or psychosis. The nurse must protect safety while preserving dignity and using the least restrictive effective response.
